chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a narrated from 'Abdillah and Ja'far and Muhammad ibn 'Abbas from 'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (the Imams), upon them be peace, who said:
The free person and the slave do not inherit from each other.

key_terms.اَلْحُرُّ: the free person (one who is not a slave)

ai.seo_question: Do free people and slaves inherit from each other in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith articulates the principle of *hijab al-kuf'* (blocking by status), where the difference in legal freedom prevents mutual inheritance between a free person and a slave. This ruling is central to Shia jurisprudence, illustrating how social status acts as a barrier to inheritance rights, distinct from the general rules of kinship. It underscores the historical legal reality where manumission was required to establish full inheritance ties.
